title: Stakeholder Orchestra Playbook and Canary Checklist (working)
content:
Purpose
This is a working playbook — a compact, operational guide for cross-functional canary rollouts and A/B tests using the "orchestra" model: small number of stewards (conductors), focused telemetry (scorecards), and a set of short, repeatable ceremonies.

Scope
- Applies to any feature or model change that touches the runtime path (generation/chat/embedding), routing rules, or traffic-slicing logic.
- Intended for medium-to-high risk rollouts where visibility + fast rollback are required.
- Not a replacement for full release docs (component owners still own deep runbooks).

High-level approach (the orchestra metaphor)
- Conductor: release steward who runs the ceremony and calls pause/abort.
- Section leads: metrics, infra, SRE/oncall, product, solutions eng (short-checkin owners).
- Scorecard: a 1-page telemetry summary (audible cues) showing latency, error rate, qualitative quality signal (human review), and cost delta.
- Pause chords (safety checks): quick, configurable thresholds that pause traffic automatically.

Ceremony (15–30 mins window at activation)
1) Pre-flight (T-72h): announcements, checklist, test traffic configured.
2) Dry-run (T-24h): smoke synthetic traffic through the canary slice, collect baseline scorecard.
3) Activation (T0): steward opens a controlled gate (1–2% traffic) and starts the live scorecard watch.
4) Rapid expansion steps: (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%) with 5–15 minute hold windows (configurable).
5) Post-mortem checkpoint (T+24–72h): capture observations, incidents, and retro items.

Roles & responsibilities (short)
- Conductor / Steward (product/PM): run ceremony, runbook checklist, final go/no-go, comms.
- Metrics lead (data/observability): owns scorecard queries, real-time dashboard.
- Infra/SRE: watch infra signals (tail latency p99/p999, GPU contention, queueing).
- Quality lead (ML researcher/Applied ML): sample outputs, human review, fuzz tests.
- Solutions/Customer Success: keep external stakeholders informed for customer-impacting changes.

Scorecard (single-sheet) — minimum columns
- Traffic slice & percent, start time
- Latency p50/p95/p99 (ms)
- Backend errors (5xx) and request errors (4xx)
- Model regressions (BLEU/ROUGE-style/embedding drift proxy) OR manual quality rating (% pass)
- Cost delta (per-token cost) and estimated monthly impact
- Key customer probes (list of 3–5 customers to watch)
- Canary health (green/amber/red) + steward note

Signal definitions and quick queries (stubs)
- Latency spike: p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.4 for 3 consecutive minutes -> amber
- Error surge: 5xx rate > baseline_5xx + 0.5% absolute -> amber
- OOM/GPU queueing: GPU_util sustained > 95% for 2 min -> red
- Quality drop: human-sampled pass rate < 85% or automated metric drop > 10% -> red

Sample SQL/metrics queries (replace metric names)
- Baseline latency: SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 95) FROM requests WHERE model='x' AND ts > now()-interval '30 minutes';
- Error rate: SELECT count_if(status >= 500)/count(*) FROM requests WHERE route='chat' AND ts > now()-interval '15 minutes';
- Customer probe: SELECT count(*) FROM requests WHERE customer_id in (123,456,789) AND ts > now()-interval '1 hour' GROUP BY status;

Canary checklist (practical, tick-box style)
- [ ] Preconditions: infra autoscaling policy validated, KV cache warmed, canary model pinned
- [ ] Synthetic smoke tests passed (latency, basic correctness)
- [ ] Scorecard dashboard deployed and shared with stakeholders
- [ ] Canary slice routing rules configured and tested (rollforward/rollback toggles present)
- [ ] Observability alerts pre-set (pager thresholds for red signals)
- [ ] Communications template drafted (Slack, email, status page snippet)
- [ ] Post-activation sample set and human reviewers assigned

Rollback & pause logic (decision grid)
- Automatic pause (immediate): infra red signals (OOM, sustained GPU saturations), catastrophic 5xx spike (>5% absolute)
- Steward immediate rollback (0–5% exposure): red quality signal OR key customer failure detected
- Fast rollback (5–20% exposure): sustained amber signals for >15 minutes without improvement
- Planned slow rollback (>=20%): coordinated rollback with infra and release manager, announce to customers if needed

Communication templates (short)
- Slack short: "Canary activation: feature X -> 5% at 2026-03-10T15:00Z. Steward: Aisha. Watch: #prod-monitoring. If GREEN at 15:15, move to 20%."
- Customer note (if impacted): "We detected a regression in feature X for a subset of traffic and paused the rollout at 5%. We're investigating and will follow up within 60 minutes."

Human review protocol (quick)
- Sampling cadence: 50 examples/minute for first 10 minutes, then 10/min for each hold period.
- Review checklist per sample: hallucination? unsafe content? correctness? formatting? score 0–2 and pass if average >=1.4

A/B test guardrails (when simultaneous with canary)
- Never run A/B with more than 2 variants plus control in a canary slice. Complexity is the enemy for early canaries.
- Ensure randomization seed is stable and replayable.
- Lock experiment metrics (primary/secondary) before activation; do not change while experiment active.

On-call integration
- Pager route for immediate red signals goes to SRE primary and metrics lead (alert message contains steward name and roll/ pause commands).
- Runbook header: quick steps to isolate canary slice, re-route traffic to fallback model, and surface logs to steward channel.

Post-mortem skeleton (for quick capture)
- What happened (timeline)
- Signals observed (links to dashboards)
- Actions taken and time to action
- Root cause hypothesis
- Follow-ups assigned (owner + due date)

Open questions / TODOs (working)
- Do we want an automated quality-scorer pipeline for embeddings drift? (Priya exploring options.)
- Should we add a "silent canary" mode that only computes metrics without affecting ranking decisions?
- How to standardize per-customer probes (template list + automated heartbeat)?

Appendix (copy/paste snippets & quick links)
- Quick expand command: curl -X POST https://console-api/_activate_canary -d '{"slice":"canary-1","pct":5}' (ops-only)
- Slack channel: #prod-monitoring, pager: SRE-runbook/team-sre
- Confluence index (linked above)

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep the ceremony lean. If we need >6 stakeholders in the active watch, we are doing it wrong.
- Empirically, 5–15 minute holds catch 75% of regressions in our last 6 rollouts. Need to re-evaluate with larger datasets.
- Next iteration: add lightweight A/B cross-breakdown in scorecard (per-user-segment).

End of doc — this is a living draft. Fill gaps above and tag items with owners.
